## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The production change in `app/report.py` is correct: only a header of exactly `REPORT v1` is now accepted, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers that check. However, one of the two added regression tests passes for an unrelated reason, so it does not protect the version check it says it guards.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` never sends a v0 header to the parser. The input `"REPORT v1\nversion=v1"` has no `END` line, and `rsplit("v1", 1)` swaps only the last `v1`, so the result is `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. `parse_report` returns `None` for it at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check (`app/report.py:3`) and never reaches the new header check at `app/report.py:5`. The comment at line 9 says the test changes "the fixture's version to v0", but it actually changes a body field. Could you use a complete fixture with a legacy header, such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or else delete the test since line 16 already covers that case? — The test would still pass if the header check were reverted to `startswith("REPORT ")` or removed, so it gives false assurance about the regression it names.

(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` (tests/test_report.py:15-17) would fail against the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check, because the old code returned `["value=ok"]` for `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`. It is a real regression test for the new check.
